problem: Fresh standard replies allocate two blocks per request; test whether owned atomic publication and direct kernel waiting produce full request improvements.
implementation: One unique producer and non-Sync receiver; one Arc allocation, acquire/release flags, owned response slot, Linux compare-and-wait futex with portable parking fallback. Detached worker, queue bounds, normal semantic dispatch, caller-buffer isolation and watchdog remain.
alternatives_considered: Keep the original standard unbounded reply channel (selected).
Previously rejected single-slot standard channel and Mutex/park-token mailbox.
Atomic one-shot owned cell (this rejected experiment).

transformations: four model tests replace ordinary test module
source_receipt.scope: Actual state transitions and endpoint/drop logic retained. Kernel syscalls, timed waits, allocator performance and full C11 behaviors are not certified by this model.

loom.limits: Portable wait model replaces libc kernel waits and timed waits; no Miri, full C11 proof or syscall-error certification.

allocation_observer.scope: Single-thread ready-before-wait System allocator diagnostic; not RSS or performance credit.

known_limits: Unexpected Linux futex-wait errors switch to portable parking but injected ENOSYS not tested.

decision_basis: SDK arrays regress mean latency 8.33% and process CPU 7.82%; all four candidate array legs are slower than neighboring baseline. Positive small/numeric and materialized native cases do not offset adverse shapes. Overlay eight/32 callers also regress mean latency 0.90%/0.70%.
interpretation: Allocation request count and bytes are sharply reduced, but dominant end-to-end costs remain. The measured mixed outcomes do not establish that allocator cost, scheduler behavior, code layout, or Python alone caused the regressions. No observer stage is subtracted as an exact latency budget.
gate_scope: 25 embedded tests (including 11 reply tests) and four portable Loom models passed. Initial two visibility compile failures retained. No full native/app release gate claimed for this rejected candidate. No Miri or syscall-error certification.
resource_scope: No persistent cache, retained reply pool, new worker or storage backend. Allocation diagnostic measured 20000 ready-before-wait 32-byte outcomes per role with System allocator, 2/1760 bytes -> 1/72 bytes per reply. RSS and timings in SDK logs are whole-process diagnostics, not isolated resource credit.
